start_here: Say to your AI: "In my folder /srv/bakery-site allow my AI command line only Read and Edit, then read the list back to me." It keeps the list in this computer's settings file and reads it back.
no_lists_because: The allowed tools are kept per folder in this computer's own settings file, not in a list of your account.
instructions: 1. Pick one existing workspace folder and the tool names you want allowed, for example Read,Edit.

2. Say "Allow Read and Edit in /srv/bakery-site". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs node tools/follow-my-ai-command-line-runs/do-work/follow-runs.mjs --allow-tools /srv/bakery-site "Read,Edit" from the Workshop checkout.
3. Read it back with --tools /srv/bakery-site (or --tools alone for every folder) and take it away with --clear-tools /srv/bakery-site.

4. A folder with no list keeps the command line's own permission rules; a command line with no allow-list flag (Codex) is answered as not applying. A folder that does not exist, or no tool named, exits 2 with {"error"} on standard error.

worked_examples.title: Allow Read and Edit in one folder, with a repeated name kept once
worked_examples.ask: In /srv/bakery-site allow my AI command line only Read and Edit.
worked_examples.given: From tools/follow-my-ai-command-line-runs/test/session-runs.test.mjs ("the workspace allow-list is kept, read and cleared by folder"), whose call setWorkspaceTools(rules, folder, 'Read, Edit,Read') is what the command runs. Command: node tools/follow-my-ai-command-line-runs/do-work/follow-runs.mjs --allow-tools /srv/bakery-site "Read, Edit,Read" (the folder must exist).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"folder":"/srv/bakery-site","tools":["Read","Edit"]} printed as pretty JSON; the test asserts the names are trimmed and the duplicate dropped. Then --tools /srv/bakery-site answers {"folder":"/srv/bakery-site","tools":["Read","Edit"]} and --clear-tools /srv/bakery-site answers {"folder":"/srv/bakery-site","cleared":true}.
